summary: Superpowers & MCP Contract — central registry of all plugins, skills, and MCP tools available to agents in this project.

plugins.name: oh-my-opencode-slim
plugins.purpose: Agent framework — provides orchestration-template, verification-before-completion skills
plugins.when_to_use: Always active. Core framework for agent behavior.

plugins.name: @razroo/opencode-model-fallback
plugins.purpose: Automatic model fallback chain — if primary model fails, falls through fallback_models list
plugins.when_to_use: Always active. Each agent has its own fallback_models list in opencode.json.

plugins.name: @zenobius/opencode-skillful
plugins.purpose: Lazy-loaded skill discovery and injection — provides skill_find, skill_use, skill_resource tools. Skills only consume tokens when explicitly loaded.
plugins.when_to_use: Use skill_find to discover skills by keyword, skill_use to load a skill into context, skill_resource to read reference files. Reduces context overhead from pre-loaded skills.

plugins.name: @tarquinen/opencode-dcp
plugins.purpose: Dynamic Context Pruning — compress, deduplicate, and purge obsolete tool outputs to reduce token usage. Replaces stale conversation content with summaries.
plugins.when_to_use: Automatic. Provides /dcp command for manual control. Complements lean-ctx compaction.

plugins.name: @morphllm/opencode-morph-plugin
plugins.purpose: Fast Apply editing (10,500+ tok/s), WarpGrep agentic codebase search, and context compaction via Morph API. Requires MORPH_API_KEY env var.
plugins.when_to_use: Use morph_edit for large file changes with scattered edits (300+ lines). Use warpgrep_codebase_search for fast agentic code search. Context compaction runs automatically.

plugins.name: @openspoon/subtask2
plugins.purpose: Extended orchestration system with granular flow control — extends /commands and subtask with more powerful delegation capabilities.
plugins.when_to_use: For complex multi-step orchestration beyond basic subtask. Extends existing subtask tool.

plugins.name: opencode-goal-plugin
plugins.purpose: Session-scoped /goal workflow that keeps objectives in context and auto-continues until complete.
plugins.when_to_use: Use /goal at session start to set a working objective. Auto-continues until goal is achieved.

plugins.name: opencode-vibeguard
plugins.purpose: Secret/PII redaction — replaces sensitive strings with placeholders before LLM requests, restores after response and before tool execution.
plugins.when_to_use: Always active. Configure patterns in vibeguard.config.json in project root.

plugins.name: opencode-websearch-cited
plugins.purpose: Web search with inline citations and Sources list — provides websearch_cited tool backed by web search providers.
plugins.when_to_use: Use when web search results need source citations. Complements built-in websearch.

plugins.name: opencode-worktree
plugins.purpose: Zero-friction git worktrees for OpenCode — isolates feature branches without switching working directory.
plugins.when_to_use: When working on multiple features simultaneously or needing isolated workspaces. Complements using-git-worktrees skill.

plugins.name: superpowers@git+https://github.com/obra/superpowers.git
plugins.purpose: 8 methodology skills for structured development: brainstorming, writing-plans, TDD, subagent-driven-dev, systematic-debugging, verification-before-completion, executing-plans, finishing-a-branch, requesting/receiving code review
plugins.when_to_use: Use `/skill <name>` to load the relevant skill before its methodology is needed.

plugins.name: opencode-notify
plugins.when_to_use: Use for operations that take >30 seconds (mvn verify, mvn clean install, etc.)

superpowers_skills.name: brainstorming
superpowers_skills.when_to_use: Before any feature creation, component building, or behavior modification

superpowers_skills.name: writing-plans
superpowers_skills.purpose: Task breakdown into 2-5 minute chunks with complete code
superpowers_skills.when_to_use: When you have a spec/requirements for a multi-step task, before touching code

superpowers_skills.name: test-driven-development
superpowers_skills.purpose: Red/green/refactor cycle — write failing test first, then implement, then refactor
superpowers_skills.when_to_use: When implementing any feature or bugfix, before writing implementation code

superpowers_skills.name: subagent-driven-development
superpowers_skills.when_to_use: When executing implementation plans with independent tasks

superpowers_skills.name: systematic-debugging
superpowers_skills.purpose: Structured root cause analysis (4 phases: reproduce, isolate, hypothesize, fix)
superpowers_skills.when_to_use: When encountering any bug, test failure, or unexpected behavior, before proposing fixes

superpowers_skills.name: verification-before-completion
superpowers_skills.purpose: Run verification commands and confirm output before claiming work is complete
superpowers_skills.when_to_use: Before committing, creating PRs, or claiming work is done

superpowers_skills.name: executing-plans
superpowers_skills.purpose: Execute written plans with batch execution and review checkpoints
superpowers_skills.when_to_use: When you have a written implementation plan to execute

superpowers_skills.name: requesting-code-review
superpowers_skills.purpose: Submit code for review before merging
superpowers_skills.when_to_use: When completing tasks, implementing major features, or before merging

superpowers_skills.name: receiving-code-review
superpowers_skills.purpose: Act on review feedback with technical rigor
superpowers_skills.when_to_use: When receiving code review feedback, before implementing suggestions

mcp_tools.name: gitnexus
mcp_tools.purpose: Code intelligence graph — 5381 symbols, 13291 relationships, 295 execution flows
key_tools: gitnexus_query({query, repo}) — Find execution flows by concept
gitnexus_context({name, repo}) — 360° view of a symbol
gitnexus_impact({target, direction, repo}) — Blast radius analysis (MANDATORY before edits)
gitnexus_detect_changes() — Verify expected scope before commit
mcp_tools.when_to_use: Before every non-trivial edit (impact), during code exploration (query/context), before commit (detect_changes)

mcp_tools.name: graphify
key_tools: graphify_get_neighbors({label}) — Direct neighbors of a node
graphify_get_community({community_id}) — All nodes in a community
mcp_tools.when_to_use: For unfamiliar code exploration (after gitnexus_query), community detection, finding cross-module relationships

mcp_tools.name: lean-ctx
mcp_tools.purpose: Memory/persistence layer — cross-session knowledge, file compression, shell execution
key_tools: lean-ctx ctx_shell — Shell execution (ONLY authorized shell tool)
lean-ctx ctx_knowledge remember/recall — Persistent knowledge storage
mcp_tools.when_to_use: Always — it's the default shell, memory, and file reading tool. Prefer over native equivalents.

mcp_tools.name: context7
mcp_tools.purpose: Library documentation retrieval — up-to-date API docs and code examples
mcp_tools.when_to_use: For libraries with frequent API changes (Spring Boot, React, AI SDKs), version-specific behavior, or unfamiliar libs

mcp_tools.name: postgres
mcp_tools.purpose: Database access — schema inspection, query execution, performance analysis
key_tools: pg_query — Full SQL queries (requires ALLOW_WRITES=1 for writes)
pg_list_tables — All tables in a schema
pg_search_columns — Find columns by name across schemas
mcp_tools.when_to_use: For database schema changes, query optimization, data migration, or investigating DB-related issues

mcp_tools.name: firecrawl
mcp_tools.purpose: Web search, scraping, and content extraction — Firecrawl MCP server provides firecrawl_* tools for all agents
key_tools: firecrawl_search({query, limit}) — Web search with full content extraction
firecrawl_scrape({url, formats}) — Single page content extraction
firecrawl_agent({prompt, urls}) — Autonomous web research agent
firecrawl_extract({urls, prompt, schema}) — Structured data extraction
firecrawl_map({url, search}) — Discover all URLs on a website
mcp_tools.when_to_use: For web search, documentation lookup, scraping, structured data extraction, competitive research, and content monitoring. All agents have firecrawl_* tools available via MCP.

startup_protocol.step_0: Create feature branch: git checkout -b feature/<YYYYMMDD>-<description>
startup_protocol.step_1: Load skills: orchestration-template → superpowers-contract → brainstorming (if creative work)
startup_protocol.step_3: Sync state: read STATE.md + PROJECT.md + lean-ctx knowledge
startup_protocol.step_4: Refresh intelligence: gitnexus analyze if stale
startup_protocol.step_5: Plugins auto-load from opencode.json plugin array. Key plugins: @zenobius/opencode-skillful (lazy skills), @tarquinen/opencode-dcp (context pruning), @morphllm/opencode-morph-plugin (fast editing), opencode-vibeguard (secret redaction)

config_files.vibeguard.config.json: Project root. Patterns for secret/PII redaction.
config_files..opencode-skillful.json: Project root. Skill discovery paths and renderer config.
config_files.MORPH_API_KEY: Environment variable. Required for @morphllm/opencode-morph-plugin. Set in ~/.zshrc: export MORPH_API_KEY='sk-...'
